description: List issues across one or more GitHub repositories. Pull requests are excluded. Every repository returns its own array of issues and its own next_cursor; send that cursor back on the same repository to read the next page.

repos.description: The repositories to read, one provider call each.

full_name.description: The repository as owner/repo, which is the option id github-list_repos-1 hands the picker. Send this, or send owner and repo.

cursor.description: The page cursor this repository returned last time. Paging is per repository, because each repository is its own provider call with its own pages.

since.description: ISO 8601, e.g. 2026-09-01T00:00:00Z. Only issues updated at or after this time come back.

response_schema.description: Lenient ingress on GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues. Reads the fields the node maps and lets GitHub keep adding the rest.

quirks.why_execute: GitHub has no endpoint that lists issues for several repositories at once, and the plural contract also has to drop pull requests and keep a cursor per repository. A declarative http mapping cannot express a fan-out with per-item results, so the work is code.
quirks.pull_requests_are_issues: The issues endpoint serves pull requests too, because GitHub counts every pull request as an issue. Only a pull request carries the `pull_request` key, so that key is the filter. Use github-list_pull_requests-1 to read the ones dropped here.
quirks.pagination: GitHub answers with a `Link` header carrying `rel="next"`, which a node cannot read: send_request hands back the parsed JSON body and nothing else. So the cursor is the page number and a full page (100 records) is the signal that another page exists. Fullness is measured on the page GitHub served, before the pull request filter.
quirks.labels_filter: GitHub takes the label filter as one comma-separated string; the node joins the array.
